# Full source parity, actual cap coverage, and a four-interval calibration

This note combines two established inputs and records their exact consequence. It proves no new numerical OC bound. In particular union coverage must not be promoted to the missing Gamma_d weighted payment.

## 1. Strict exclusion of other actual deepest marks

Use the attained pure outward-smoothed problem with positive width h, compact positive fibers, proper own cores and the full-normal identity. Let Y_i=(p_i,y_i) be its distinct deepest marks. For an actual cap N=(a,u) at Y_i, write c=N·Y_i and Q(N,c) for its raw smoothed mass. Its own strip has positive coarea.

For j different from i one has

    N·(Y_j−Y_i)<0.                                      (1)

Indeed Q(N,N·Y_j) cannot be smaller than the common deepest value. If N·Y_j>c, strict decrease of Q immediately to the right of c, supplied by the positive own coarea, makes that impossible; monotonicity then treats larger threshold differences as well. If equality holds, the SAME normalized cap and threshold are active at both marks. Its full-normal identity

    m−A(0,Sigma u)=S Y

has the same m,A,S,u at each mark, and S>0. It forces Y_i=Y_j, a contradiction.

For any finite positive raw balanced menu at i, sum rho_l u_l=0. Consequently its averaged base normal a_bar_i=sum rho_l a_l satisfies

    a_bar_i·(p_j−p_i)<0,  j≠i.                         (2)

This is an actual exposing normal supplied by EVERY raw balanced menu, rather than a separately chosen geometric exposer.

If every cap in that menu has zero transition-strip coarea on another full-dimensional fiber K_z, its continuous smoothed integrand is constant zero or one there. Otherwise continuity on the connected interior would give an open set with intermediate integrand and positive strip coarea. Continuity then extends the constant to the boundary. In particular (1) forces every cap to miss the ENTIRE fiber at every other deepest base: a fully captured fiber would give nonnegative margin at its deepest mark.

## 2. The terminating parity forest and a menu-independent root

Let P be the finite lattice-complete positive base set. Let I={p_i} satisfy

    conv(I) intersect Z^n=I,

with distinct parities. These are already proved properties of the pure smooth deepest set. Suppose moreover that I occupies EVERY parity occupied by P. For z in P choose p(z) in I with its parity and set

    T(z)=(z+p(z))/2.

This is an integer point in P by convexity and lattice completeness. If z is outside conv(I),

    dist(T(z),conv(I))<=dist(z,conv(I))/2.

Because P is finite, iteration reaches conv(I) in finitely many steps, and hence reaches a source p_i. Make the parity choice once; the resulting root i(z) is independent of menus.

Expanding the midpoint iterations gives p_i as a convex combination of the original z, with strictly positive dyadic coefficient, and source points. Move any self coefficient at p_i to the left and divide. For z not in I this yields

    p_i=lambda z+sum_{j≠i}lambda_j p_j,
    lambda>0, lambda_j>=0, lambda+sum lambda_j=1.       (3)

At least one lambda_j is positive, since z≠p_i. Applying (2) to (3) shows

    a_bar_i·(z−p_i)>0.                                (4)

For EVERY x in R^d, the raw weighted sum of its menu margins at base z is the left side of (4). Thus at least one menu cap strictly contains (z,x). If every outside fiber has zero coarea for these caps, at least one cap captures the entire K_z.

This recovers a genuine source-group cover from the saturated parity hypothesis, while retaining the actual active caps and their continuous coordinates. It gives no lower bound Gamma_d on the response weight of the captured caps. The forest and its dyadic relations are archived arithmetic tools; the contribution here is their precise combination with the strict actual-cap margin and zero-coarea properties.

## 3. Positive saturation deficit can survive all these hypotheses

Take n=d=1, bases −1,0,1,2, with fibers

    K_-1=[−5/4,−21/20],  K_0=[−1,1],
    K_1=[−3/4,3/4],     K_2=[−7/40,7/40].             (5)

Their lengths are 1/5,2,3/2,7/20. The lower endpoint increments are 1/4,1/4,23/40, hence nondecreasing; the upper increments are 41/20,−1/4,−23/40, hence nonincreasing. Their linear interpolations define an actual planar convex body with exactly these integer fibers.

Let sigma>0 be the square root of its actual pooled within-fiber variance. For the uniform outward kernel use width w=h sigma and assume 0<w<1/20. By homogeneity every nonvertical cap may be written with continuous normal +1 or −1. Put

    Y_0=(0,−1/10),  Y_1=(1,0),
    Q=11/10+w/2.                                    (6)

For a proper cut through y in an interval, the +1 own cap has length upper−y+w/2, and the −1 cap has length y−lower+w/2. All cuts below remain uniformly proper.

At Y_0, a +1 cap with base tilt a=−9/10 misses every outside fiber, with margins at most −1/20. Its own mass is Q. Outside mass is always nonnegative, so no +1 cap has smaller mass. For a −1 cap, if a<=19/20 the whole left fiber is captured; if a>19/20 the whole fiber K_1 is captured. Thus its outside mass is at least 1/5 for EVERY base tilt. A sufficiently negative tilt captures only K_-1 outside, attaining that value. Its own mass is 9/10+w/2, so again the minimum is Q.

All actual minimizing caps at Y_0 are saturated outside. For +1, minimum outside mass zero forces every outside integrand to vanish. For −1, the alternative a>19/20 has outside mass at least 3/2>1/5. In the other alternative K_-1 is fully captured, so equality forces every remaining outside integrand to vanish.

At Y_1, for either continuous orientation, if a>=7/40 the entire right fiber K_2 is captured. If a<7/40, the ordinary contribution from K_0 alone exceeds 33/40>7/20: when −1<=a<7/40 its cap length is 1−a, and for a<−1 it is the full length two. Outward smoothing can only increase it. Therefore every cap has outside mass at least 7/20. A sufficiently positive base tilt captures K_2 and misses both left fibers, attaining the bound. Adding the own mass 3/4+w/2 gives exactly Q for both signs. Equality again forces saturated outside integrands.

Pure-base caps containing Y_0 or Y_1 have masses at least 11/5 and 37/20 respectively, so they are inactive. To verify global deepestness without restricting candidate points, freeze the two active caps at each mark. Moving upward in its own fiber strictly decreases the +1 cap until its own contribution vanishes; moving downward strictly decreases the −1 cap. The outside contribution cannot increase under either threshold move. This proves that each displayed point uniquely maximizes depth on its fiber. At the two exposed endpoint bases a pure-base cap isolates the whole endpoint fiber, of mass at most 7/20<Q. Hence I={0,1} is the COMPLETE deepest base set, occupying both parities.

Nevertheless the pure-base outside baseline at source zero is

    B_0=min(1/5,3/2+7/20)=1/5.

Every positive-orientation active cap there has outside mass zero, giving strictly positive saturation deficit B_0−Q_out=1/5. Every balanced menu at that source uses both orientations. Thus full source parity and zero outside coarea do NOT force a zero-deficit menu. The d=1 response weights are one half, so the ordinary hinge field already pays Gamma_1; this example obstructs only the proposed stronger saturation inference.

All claims concern every real base tilt and both continuous orientations. In dimension one these exhaust all nonvertical ambient halfspaces; pure-base closed halfspaces were checked separately. The example is not below OC and introduces no counterexample to the desired theorem.
